, this mechanism leverages both bidirectional cross-attention and a linear gate to enable reciprocal enhancement. Specifically, deep semantic information from ProtT5 embeddings strengthens the secondary structure characterization, while local conformational details from the secondary structure, in turn, provide the embeddings with rich structural information. The features are then passed through the linear gating unit, which dynamically adjusts and combines the information flow from the two modalities for efficient and adaptable fusion.
the standard attention mechanism, specifically designed to model the interdependencies between two heterogeneous feature sequences
enables one feature sequence, acting as the Query, to dynamically aggregate relevant information from another sequence, which serves as the Key and Value, thereby facilitating cross-modal alignment.

Specifically, the bidirectional interaction is driven by two explicit information flows. In the ProtT5-to-ss8 flow, ss8 features act as the Query, and ProtT5 embeddings serve as the Key and Value, enabling structural features to integrate global semantic context. Conversely, in the ss8-to-ProtT5 flow, ProtT5 embeddings query ss8 features to incorporate local structural cues. These dual pathways facilitate effective alignment between semantic and structural representations.

This study introduces NeuroPpred-PSCG, a multimodal deep learning framework for neuropeptide identification.
The model architecture integrates information across different scales.

Through the application of a bidirectional cross-attention mechanism and a multi-scale gated convolutional network, it harmonizes the high-level semantic insights captured by the ProtT5 language model with the localized structural patterns defined by secondary structures, thus facilitating a hierarchical analysis of the sequence.
Our method achieves consistent improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods in overall performance.
ablation results highlight the importance of the multimodal fusion strategy for model performance. Additional evaluations of
robustness and generalization, together with visualization analyses, show that the model remains stable and captures biologically meaningful patterns.
Overall, this study highlights the potential of multimodal deep fusion in characterizing complex biological sequences, offering a promising approach for the discovery of bioactive peptides.
